Body:
Tim Hortons may be a Canadian legend, but its charming Katy outpost feels right at home in the Texas suburbs. Tucked into a quiet corner of town, this cozy café offers a nostalgic, no-fuss approach to coffee and baked treats—a welcome change from trend-heavy cafés.

Famous across Canada for its reliable drip coffee, donuts, Timbits, and breakfast staples, Tim Hortons brings a touch of northern comfort to Katy. The hot coffee here is simple and satisfying, especially when paired with a tender cake donut dusted lightly with nutmeg—perfect for dunking. While some of the other donuts leaned a bit dry, the holiday flavors and assortment of baked goods still add to the fun.

The menu also features savory options, including avocado toast, which was just okay but offered balance among all the sweets. With festive seasonal beverages and classic cold brews available, there’s something for every type of coffee drinker.

The café’s interior is small but warm and inviting, infused with Canadian-themed décor that adds to its charm. Service is decent, though the drive-thru can get chaotic—making the dine-in experience the better choice.

Tim Hortons in Katy is a sweet little gem for a cozy winter morning, a donut-and-coffee break, or a quick suburban caffeine fix. And with more locations on the horizon, Texans may soon enjoy even more of Canada’s favorite grab-and-go coffee spot.

Must-Try Items:

Hot drip coffee

Cake donut (nutmeg-kissed, tender, perfect for dunking)

Seasonal/holiday drinks

Cold brew vanilla (if you’re in the mood for something chilled)

Review

Sara I. (Dec 5, 2022):

“Such a great little gem of a coffee shoppe tucked in a quiet corner within the suburbs of Katy, TX.

Tim Horton's is originally from Canada.. & is all the rage up in the northern hemisphere... & I can totally see why! It is considered Canada's favorite coffee on the run. This spot specializes in both hot and cold coffee drinks, as well as donuts, pastries and a few savory items.

Had heard about Tim Hortons back in the day.. just hadn't ventured out to Canada in awhile. I am glad we have a location here in TX, which is soon to spread out within neighboring cities.

Hot coffee was great.. nice and simple. Drip coffee paired with a donut? Keeping it old school. I didn't care for any cold bevvie that day.. but my friend's cold brew vanilla drink looked good. Plenty of holiday flavors this time of the year as well.

They have a variety of donuts to choose from.. my favorite being the cake donut. Tender and sprinkled a bit with nutmeg. Dunk it into hot coffee.. bliss. The other donuts were on the drier side & didn't taste fresh. That's too bad because this spot specializes in their sweet treats. Also tried their avocado toast which was just okay. I'm glad they have a bit of savory items to balance with all the sweetness.

Interior is quite small.. but cozy. Decor is quite heartwarming and very Canadian. Service was okay.. could be better. Their drive thru seemed chaotic and I totally recommend visiting the interior of the cafe.

All in all, a great spot to set up shoppe. I'll definitely revisit in the near future. Here's hoping we can get more Hortons on the way.. because ‘Horton hears a who! & A why not?!’ Lol. Totally a Dr Seuss reference.. if you know, you know. Cheers and happy coffee drinking during the coziest month of the year!”

In-N-Out Burger remains one of those rare fast-food spots where simplicity truly shines—and the Stafford location captures that charm perfectly. Fast, friendly service and a straightforward menu keep things easy, while the consistently fresh ingredients make each visit reliably satisfying.

The classic hamburger is the star here: a single beef patty, fresh toppings, and a toasted bun that hits every nostalgic note. Adding grilled onions and chopped peppers elevates the flavor without losing the simplicity that defines In-N-Out. While the fries are admittedly polarizing, requesting them extra crispy gives them that golden, crunchy finish many diners prefer. Shakes are thick, creamy, and nostalgic—especially when ordered Neapolitan style, a fun little secret-menu option.

Always buzzing with energy, this location brings color and movement to the Stafford area and satisfies burger cravings day and night. It’s a dependable go-to for simple, flavorful comfort—especially during the cozy months when a warm burger just feels right.

Fries extra crispy

Neapolitan shake (secret menu)

Animal-style fries for sauce lovers

Cozy, welcoming, and full of personality, this Thai eatery stands out not just for its bold dishes but also for the heartfelt conversations and charm offered by its owners. Friendly, talkative, and deeply accommodating, they make guests feel like neighbors rather than customers—an experience that lingers long after the meal ends.

The food is lively, fragrant, and crafted with care. Fresh red chilies—not just ground spice—give many dishes their signature punch. The pad thai is refreshingly light and crisp, leaning into a Northern Thai style that departs from the heavier, greasier versions often found elsewhere. This variation highlights brightness and texture over oiliness.

The penang curry is another standout: bubbling hot, aromatic, creamy with coconut milk, and filled with a variety of vegetables. The vegetarian version hits all the right notes, though the menu offers plenty of meat-based curries worth exploring next time. Together, these dishes showcase Naha Thai’s commitment to freshness, balance, and bold flavor.

With plans to return for soups, teas, and more, this spot easily becomes a favorite for Thai lovers in the area. An inviting setting, flavorful food, and warm conversation—Naha Thai gives Sugar Land exactly the spice and comfort it needed.

Pad Thai (light, crisp & Northern Thai–inspired)

Penang curry (aromatic, creamy, veggie-packed)

Any dish featuring their fresh red chilies

Body:
Flower Child has long been admired for bringing a vibrant, West Coast–inspired, health-forward dining experience to Houston. With its colorful bowls, sustainable ingredients, vegetarian-friendly menu, and sunny ambiance, it quickly became a favorite for those craving fresh, wholesome meals. But over the years, the experience has shifted.

Where Flower Child once delivered generous portions layered with bold flavors, crisp vegetables, and nourishing grains, recent visits reveal smaller servings and a noticeable decrease in toppings—turning bowls that once felt abundant into meals that leave diners wanting more.

Still, the menu retains its charm: forbidden rice bowls, ancient grain creations, sweet potato accents, nutritious greens, and a highly flexible lineup of vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-free options. The atmosphere remains bright, breezy, and uplifting, perfectly suited for a casual lunch, post-gym bite, or a feel-good dinner.

With strong potential and a loyal customer base, Flower Child continues to be a beloved spot—one that could easily return to greatness with a revival of the generous, well-balanced portions it once offered.

Highlights:

Vibrant, West Coast–inspired healthy bowls

Vegan-, vegetarian-, and gluten-free–friendly

Fresh ingredients, colorful presentation

Spacious seating & warm ambiance

Great variety: bowls, salads, wraps, plates, teas & more

Reviews

Sara I. Updated Review (Jul 17, 2022)

“Portions have drastically decreased at this restaurant... I ordered the mother earth bowl and only had 2 pieces of sweet potato in the bowl. I remember eating this specific item a few years ago and having more volume in the meal. They used to add more avocado and sweet potato.

Today, all I had was a measly 1 sliver of avocado and 2 chunks of sweet potato. How does anyone get full from that? Especially when it's a vegan meal to begin with... What happened Flower Child?

This restaurant was absurdly busy today, I'm assuming they're cutting corners and just not providing great meals as they used to. Everyone else enjoyed their food today; but they all agreed that it was just an ‘okay’ experience. Flower Child should consider opening up more locations. Maybe that could help.. I don't know.

All I can say is that meals should be provided with ample substance and not appear lackluster. Overpriced and it's mostly a self-serving restaurant. Fetch your own drinks and cutlery. Totally left feeling hungry.”

Sara I. Previous Review (Sep 26, 2018)

“I absolutely adore the food and the environment at Flower Child. Everything here is made fresh with a kick and snap. The menu is totally vegan friendly with a strong emphasis on using local and sustainable ingredients. There are a few meat selections that you can choose from, such as chicken, salmon, and steak. Tofu is a nice addition as well if you're into non-based meat. Thankfully, they have zero pork items here which makes me feel very comfortable.

I absolutely adore the menu; it has a strong West Coast influence and Houston was in dire need of a concept like this. It's the kind of grub that makes my belly happy and leaves me floating on cloud nine.

We visited on a cloudy Sunday afternoon, and to our surprise, the tiny line went quick and all the staff were kind and helpful. Our food didn't take long to make and was served warm and fresh.

I ordered the forbidden rice bowl with salmon as my choice of protein. I loved the savoury Asian inspired flavors that contained black pearl rice and many crisp vegetables. The mother earth is another item that I really liked. The ancient grains went very well with the sweet potatoes that were smothered in a red pepper miso vinaigrette. The broccoli pesto was vividly green and paired nicely with the leafy greens and avocado. All in all, every item danced well together in a beautiful and colorful layout.

Flower Child has salads, plates, bowls and wraps to choose from. Their drinks look great as well. I can imagine revisiting during the cooler season and wrapping around some hot tea and a warm bowl. Welcome to the city of Houston, Flower Child! I look forward to meeting you again. Until next time.”

The Asiatown Crawl at Westcroft Center brought together warmth, culture, and good company—everything that makes a community food gathering memorable. This intimate event blended laughter, storytelling, and shared heritage while exploring the local gems tucked within Sharpstown’s vibrant Asiatown. With stops ranging from ice cream shops to bakeries to a specialty market, the experience was equal parts delicious and enriching.

Guests enjoyed sweet treats, friendly conversations, and the chance to learn about Middle Eastern pastries, teas, and traditions. It was a nostalgic afternoon that felt both comforting and exciting—one of those gatherings where the people make the moments just as special as the food.

Event Highlights:

Guided cultural insights and storytelling throughout the crawl

Sweet ice creams and milkshakes to kick off the experience

Warm, inviting bakery offering saffron tea, knafeh, butter cookies & baklava

Market visit with saffron, tea biscuits & regional goods

A cozy, laid-back gathering with friends old and new

No frou frou or weird vibes whatsoever. Just chill laid-back moments. Mike ended up surprising me and that made my day. Lou, as usual, was a great host.

I co-hosted a bit of the event and loved sharing the cultural background of the food as well as the local ice cream shop, bakery, and market we visited. It is my absolute pleasure to bring rich cultural heritage and perspective thrown into the mix.

We had such a great time noshing on some sweet ice cream and milkshakes. The café blends coffeehouse culture with a diverse, globally inspired menu, offering everything from pizzas and tamales to soups, pastries, and vegan-friendly fare. That said, service quality seems to vary, and billing issues have been noted—making it important for guests to double-check receipts and remain aware during checkout. When Brasil is at its best, it’s comforting, flavorful, and quintessentially Montrose; but consistency in customer care would elevate the experience significantly.

Review

Sara I. (Jan 21, 2020):

“I’ve been visiting this café for well over a decade and things really haven’t changed much. I recently visited twice, thinking the service was top-notch. I don’t know why they’d have the audacity to charge customers for items they didn’t order. It’s a nuisance to revisit the café just to find out what happened. Be careful—ask for a receipt and make sure they don’t swipe your card twice.

I’ve always enjoyed the pizzas and tamales here. The soups are not bad, and there are many vegetarian and vegan options, which is a plus. Their café au lait is one of my favorites, served in a tall glass just like in European cafés. I always ask for maple syrup—it makes the drink feel even cozier. Sitting outside on the patio in good weather or inside the dim café is equally nice. The atmosphere appeals to me because it feels casual yet chic. It’s one of the originals in this part of town—no try-hard factor. Lots of diverse food and drink options; it’s a quick choice that keeps your belly warm and full. Body:
Black Bear Diner in Sugar Land wraps guests in a warm, nostalgic embrace—bringing the forested charm of Northern California straight into Texas. With its woodsy décor, whimsical bear accents, and comforting diner energy, it feels like stepping inside a storybook lodge. Since opening in 2019, this spot has become a beloved local go-to for families, brunch groups, and anyone craving hearty comfort food served with genuine hospitality.

The menu is extensive, offering everything from savory breakfast plates to sweet treats and classic diner staples. Service is consistently warm, even during high-traffic weekends when crowds spill out the door. Though the food can occasionally be hit-or-miss during busy waves, the overall experience remains cozy, familiar, and cherished by many.

Must-Try Items:

Patty melt (on a good day, savory and classic)

Warm, tender pancakes

Omelets & hot breakfast plates

Sweet, creamy hot chocolate

Desserts & comforting diner sides

Review

Sara I. (Jan 16, 2024): 

“BBD... aka Black Bear Diner.. such a cozy spot that reminds me of GoldiLocks and the three bears... except this bear theme is originating from Nor'Cal. Hence the theme of alll the northern trees and Nor'Cal Diner Vibes.. and yes.. some of my favorite diners are in California (my HomeState).

On with the food. This spot has been tucked away within the land of Sugar since 2019.. I've been visiting since then and have always enjoyed the grub at BBD. Albeit, there are some days when the food’s perfectly on par, and then on some days when it's just okay.

Within my most recent visit... lines were out the door, frigid air was kickin' in and groups of folks were simmering within the cozy diner. Thankfully a group of us were seated promptly and found good seats closer to the entrance. Due to the fact they were busy.. it seemed the food was just okay this time. I ordered a beef patty melt with fries and coleslaw. Fries were blonde in color, cold, and such few. Patty melt was okay. Pancakes were warm and tender as they typically are. With such a huge crowd on the weekends, food can be subpar at times.

Other than that, I have always appreciated BBD's expansive menu. Their hot chocolate is sweet, warm and creamy, and their desserts are quite nice as well. Savory hot items such as their omelets and other sandwiches are typically good.

Dining experience and service? Great. BBD has a nostalgic, woodsy, Nor'Cal feel that will make any nature enthusiast appreciative of their whimsical theme of all things bears and forests. They even sell a few bear plushies, socks, and all cuddlesy stuff at the front (where you pay). Service has always been warm and appreciative. Servers almost always check up on you. Though, they ought to put table numbers or order numbers on the table. At least twice during the weekend rush they brought out wrong food orders to our table.

All in all, this is a spot that many cherish. Perf for families, friends and groups of folk that wanna chat over coffee, pancakes and all the sweeter things in life. Until next time!”

Tucked into a calm corner of Sugar Creek Plaza, Pythagoras Conscious Food Philosophy brings warmth, creativity, and a global twist to Sugar Land’s dining scene. With its soothing ambiance, friendly service, and unexpectedly diverse vegan menu, this spot welcomes everyone—from full-time vegans to anyone who enjoys fresh, vibrant, plant-forward meals.

The menu is impressively varied, offering pizzas, soups, salads, and even Persian-inspired dishes that celebrate bold, comforting flavors. It’s the kind of place where you can settle in with friends, share a colorful spread, and leave feeling both nourished and pleasantly full.

Whether you're exploring vegan cuisine or seeking a cozy neighborhood hangout with thoughtful food, Pythagoras proves that plant-based dining can be soulful, satisfying, and deeply delicious.

Loaded vegan nachos with crisp toppings & flavorful vegan cheese

Sesame bread served with Persian-style eggplant dip

Crispy-crust pizzas with generous toppings & surprisingly delicious vegan cheese

Grapefruit sparkling drink or fresh juices

Review

Sara I. (Jul 6, 2022):

“Such a cozy little spot! I'm liking this conscious food philosophy on a quiet yet nonchalant corner of Sugar Creek plaza. I've always liked this little part of town and Pythagoras vegan cafe is a warm and bright welcome in the area. I met up with friends this evening and we all enjoyed our meals.

Despite the menu being primarily of vegan food choices; there really is something for everyone here. The menu is chock full of pizza choices, soups, salads and Persian food items. We started with their loaded vegan nachos as an appetizer and it was quite filling and crisp. Plenty of veggies and the vegan cheese doused on top had a good flavor. Nachos were light and a great sharing item with friends.

Delish. As well as their pizzas; the crust is crispy and the toppings are generous. I'm typically not a fan of vegan cheese, but theirs is quite good.

I recommend their grapefruit sparkling drink (non-alcoholic) or their juices. It's great to have a new vegan food joint in the area. The theme of the restaurant is unique and their service was warm and efficient. Our waiter was friendly, communicative and often checked up on us.

Thanks dear Pythagoras for enlightening our minds on a random summer evening. It's just simple Pythagorean math; our bellies were full and our hearts felt warm. What more would you want?”

Antique wooden furniture, including ottomans and dresser cabinets

Body:
The Koreatown HTX Foodie Adventure brought together friends, flavor, and cultural exploration in one seamlessly organized event. Focused on Korean cuisine and ending with a lively wander through HMart, this meetup blended education, great food, and community bonding into a memorable Sunday experience.

The highlight of the outing was a delicious Shabu-style meal—vegetarian for some, seafood and meat options for others—all seasoned with the bold sauces, spices, and banchan that define comforting Korean cooking. Each guest had their own personal hot pot setup, complete with adjustable heat controls, making the meal both engaging and customizable. Service was attentive throughout, creating a smooth, enjoyable dining experience.

After the meal, a group shopping adventure through HMart added an extra layer of fun. From rambutan to fresh nectarines to unique pantry items, everyone found something to spark curiosity. The outing wrapped with goodie bags, laughter, and the joy of reconnecting with familiar faces.

Event Highlights:

Personalized Shabu hot pot with vegetarian, seafood & meat options

Flavorful sauces, banchan & herbs

Attentive service and smooth event hosting

Post-meal grocery exploration at HMart

Fun finds: rambutan, nectarines & specialty items

Catching up with beloved community members

A cozy, flavorful, community-centered Sunday

Review

Sara I. (Aug 27, 2023):

“What a wonderful event. All things Korean food and stopping at HMART as the last part of the adventure tour! I remember when Shabu style food was mentioned — I was already intrigued from the get-go. Because of it having a Korean flair I knew that I would enjoy the food, simply because of the sauces, spice and many different condiments (banchan) veggies and herbs. Body:
Golden Dumpling House is the definition of a hidden gem—small, unassuming, and deeply rooted in the craft of traditional dumpling-making. Their offerings lean classic and comforting: thick, chewy wrappers, generously packed fillings, and that signature burst of steam when you bite in. While dine-in may be limited, their to-go dumplings travel well and arrive piping hot, making this an easy go-to for a cozy night in.

Beyond dumplings, you’ll find crisp scallion pancakes, simple sauces, and a menu of home-style dishes that reflect a no-frills, flavor-first approach. Cash-only, but worth every penny.

Must-Try Items

Steamed Chicken Dumplings – tender filling wrapped in chewy, old-world–style dough

Pan-Fried Beef Dumplings – crisp bottoms, juicy interior, deeply savory

Scallion Pancakes – house-made, crispy, and far superior to frozen versions

Black Vinegar Dumpling Sauce – the best complement to the hearty fillings

Review

Sara I. (Apr 29, 2021): 

“Golden Dumpling House seems to serve up some rather mean—actually, cute and authentic—dumplings. They’re doughy, chewy, and filled to the brim. Inside each dumpling is a hefty meatball-like center brimming with flavor. The texture is very old world, and they are super boiling hot when you nosh on them. Fresh at its best.

My favorites are the steamed chicken dumplings and the pan-fried beef dumplings—sealed with flavor and great texture. The chili sauce has way too much oil and not enough heat, but the black vinegar sauce is solid. I do wish they offered a plain shrimp and chive dumpling since not everyone eats pork; seafood dumplings would be a great addition.

The scallion pancakes are crispy and clearly house-made—nothing like the flat freezer versions you find elsewhere. Orders take about 20–25 minutes to prepare, so call ahead, and make sure to order by 7:30 pm if you’re picking up in the evening. Service was chill and prompt. Cash only.

They’ve got plenty on the menu besides dumplings, and I’ll definitely revisit to try more. Support local mom-and-pop shops—these folks put soul into their craft.”

Yummy’s Hot Chicken takes the ever-popular hot chicken trend and elevates it with a bold Syrian twist. This unassuming food truck delivers layers of flavor, crunch, and spice that set it apart from the typical fried-chicken lineup. The menu may be small, but each item is crafted with intention—crispy textures, vibrant toppings, and spice levels that range from gentle heat to full-on fire.

The chicken stays remarkably juicy beneath its golden crust, and the bright slaw adds a refreshing snap that balances the richness. Fans of creative comfort food will appreciate the unique touches, including Middle Eastern-inspired seasoning blends and their standout curry fries. Grab your order early, especially in hot weather—the food is worth savoring before the Houston heat kicks in.

Must-Try Items

Syrian Hot Chicken Sandwich (medium spice recommended) – crisp, fresh, full of layered flavor

Curry Fries – fragrant curry sauce blended with cheese; hot, bold, and delicious

Chicken Tender Basket – same addictive seasoning in tender form

Challah Bun Option – soft, slightly sweet, and a perfect match for the heat

Review

Sara I. (Aug 16, 2020): 

“Hot. Crispy. Chicken sandwich. But with a Syrian twist.

This sandwich was hecka good—lots of flavor, layers, and textures. Yummy’s has a small, simple menu, but every item overdelivers. I rarely eat anything fried, but their unique twist puts this sandwich in a league of its own. The slaw is bright and vibrant, and the chicken crust is crisp and golden.

They offer different spice levels; I chose medium and it was just right. The curry fries were surprisingly delicious—an interesting fusion with curry sauce meshed into mild cheese sauce, and they arrived steaming hot. My sandwich came on a challah bun instead of a pretzel bun, and I loved it. Definitely ask which bun they’re using.

Everything was crisp and yummy. This spot packs heat and taste. I’ll probably revisit in the fall—eating outside in summer was an adventure in itself! Thanks, Yummy’s. Hope y’all continue to thrive in the Galleria food truck park.”

Body:
Terry Hershey Park is one of Houston’s most beloved green escapes—an expansive, tree-lined sanctuary tucked right into the bustle of the Energy Corridor. With multiple entrances that each lead to different winding paths, bridges, and leafy tunnels, the park feels both vast and intimate, offering something for walkers, runners, bicyclists, and nature lovers alike.

Its long corridors of trees create shaded pathways that stretch for miles, making it easy to get wonderfully lost in the scenery. Hidden pockets of charm appear throughout the park, from neighborhood-adjacent corners to community-decorated benches and even a tiny outdoor library where visitors can borrow or leave a book. Seasonal beauty shines here—especially in spring and autumn, when wildflowers glow and cooler air turns afternoon walks into something magical.

Whether you're seeking movement, fresh air, or a peaceful reset, Terry Hershey Park remains a treasured reminder of nature’s resilience within Houston’s “concrete jungle.”

Must-Enjoy Experiences:

Long, winding tree-canopied trails

Bridges connecting different sections of the park

Jogging, cycling & long-distance walking corridors

Hidden neighborhood corners with charming touches (like a mini library!)

Seasonal scenery—especially spring wildflowers and autumn strolls

Reviews

Sara I. (May 25, 2022): “A rather large yet cozy park smacked in the middle of the energy corridor. There are various entrances to reach this park; & yet each entrance happens to guide you through a unique path. I love the large stretched out corridors here. These are tunnels that are full of trees that stretch so far out into various pathways and bridges. Great for those that are joggers or bicyclists. I find myself mostly walking here and yet I can't seem to finish the trail. It's easy to get lost here as well. Lol. Unless you spot a map or something.

As mentioned, the trails are long and unwinding. I had always known about this park yet its entrances were mysterious, and easily missed. Frequently visiting and being near the beltway, I was able to spot one of the main entrances and that was it. I've been a frequent stroller here for the past 2 years.

This park seems to have been here forever; I hope it stays & that it continues to preserve itself within the midst of the concrete jungle. There are vast neighborhoods tucked within the corners of some of the pathways. One of the neighbors decorated a bench and left a mini library outside so walkers can grab books & leave a book as well. It's these little things that are precious & that have made this park ever so charming.

I love visiting in Autumn and Spring in particular. Last year I spotted a field of yellow flowers. Just nothing but pure yellow gold all around, as if the sun had dipped its beams into the earth. Support local parks, walk, bike or jog. Or bring your fluffy best friend. Just move a bit and you'll be good! Toodles!”

Body:
Voodoo Doughnut brings its signature pink flair and eccentric personality to Houston—but the experience doesn’t quite match the magic of its flagship locations in Portland or Austin. While the shop is undeniably fun, colorful, and great for hosting out-of-town visitors, the freshness and texture of the doughnuts can be inconsistent compared to their busier, higher-volume counterparts.

Houston is full of standout donut shops, many of which offer simple, fresh, reliable classics. Voodoo leans heavily into novelty toppings and funky combinations—sometimes fun, sometimes too over the top. Yet in the middle of that theatrical menu, the simplest donuts end up being the unexpected stars.

What to Expect

Playful, quirky donut names and bright pink-themed décor

Less foot traffic = less frequent fresh batches

Best items tend to be the classic, uncomplicated donuts

Good hot coffee to pair with your picks

Review

Sara I. (Mar 21, 2020): 

“The doughnuts here aren’t as fresh as the Austin location. They’re not churning through batches the way they do in PDX or ATX, so things get a bit stale. The storefront lacks the charm of the original shops too. Houston has so many great donut spots—and this one just isn’t it for me.

I do enjoy the quirky pink aesthetic and their fun, funky donut names. Definitely a cute place to take visitors. But many toppings are overkill; more hype than substance. The jelly donut was the standout—full of raspberry jelly with a crisp, thick shell. The plain cake donut was another favorite: nutmeg-kissed, dense, not too sweet. The buttermilk bar was good as well. Basically, the simpler the flavor, the better it tasted.

Voodoo is supposed to be magically delicious, but things are getting stale—literally. On the bright side, the coffee is good, warm, local, and fresh. Ask for milk and pair it with your fave donut.

Overall? Probably won’t be back anytime soon.”

Body:
Bevers Kitchen & Gifts captures everything you want from a countryside eatery—warm hospitality, hearty homestyle dishes, and a dessert selection that will make any pie lover swoon. Located along a charming street lined with small, local shops, this cozy kitchen is the perfect mid-road-trip stop or weekend getaway treat.

Arriving just an hour before closing still left plenty of time to enjoy a light meal and some unforgettable pie. The savory menu brings comfort in every bite, especially the standout beef chili. Though beanless, this version delivers depth, warmth, and rich earthy spices that evoke true Texas comfort. Paired with wild rice seasoned with thyme, celery, and carrots, it makes a beautifully balanced and hearty bowl.

The beef brisket sandwich also earns praise—tender, flavorful, and exactly what you’d hope for from a small-town kitchen. But the real crown jewels here are the pies. From classic buttermilk to coconut cream with a towering meringue, each slice hits the mark with crisp crusts, balanced sweetness, and nostalgic charm.

Bevers Kitchen shines in its sweets, its simplicity, and its welcoming country vibe. A must-stop for anyone passing through Chappell Hill.

Must-Try Items:

Beef chili (deep, earthy, & richly spiced)

Wild rice side (herbaceous & comforting)

Beef brisket sandwich

Coconut cream pie with meringue

Buttermilk pie (classic & nostalgic)

Review

Sara I. (Mar 30, 2023): 

“What a wonderful and cozy homestyle kitchen in the countryside. I loved it here and loved everything about Bevers Kitchen & Gifts. Arrived here close to one hour before closing and had enough time to snack on some pie and a bit of savory food. Had decent leftovers because I just wanted a light bite to eat that mid-afternoon.

I loved their beef chili! I typically can't stand chili without beans, I don't want to eat beef bolognese! But theirs? Even without the beans the chili was darn good. Lots of savory and deep earthy spices. I decided to pair my chili with a side of wild rice. The wild rice was great! Earthy as well, with a tone of ground thyme and diced celery as well as carrot. Paired well with the spicy beef chili. Yum.

I liked their beef brisket sandwich as well, which I got to try a bite from my partner. The service was friendly and chill, so was the environment. It's also nestled within a cozy street full of little shops that are unique to the area.

Having a sweet tooth, I was impressed with the pies at Bevers kitchen. Hadn't had buttermilk pie in eons. Coconut cream pie with meringue.. good stuff. I was afraid the meringue would be sickly sweet. Nope. The meringue was piled high and cut well with the creaminess of the coconut cream. The pie crust? Absolute crisp. They shine with their sweets and I'll definitely revisit to try another pie when in the area. This spot is recommended by Sara the pastry gal. Go!”

The ROYCE’ Chocolate tasting event in Chinatown offered a creamy, dreamy escape into the world of premium Japanese confections. Known for its ultra-smooth textures and high-quality ingredients sourced from northern Japan, ROYCE’ brings the spirit of Hokkaido’s celebrated dairy culture straight into Houston — and this event showcased the very best of it.

Matcha nama chocolate stole the spotlight—earthy, bittersweet, and beautifully balanced with the creaminess that ROYCE’ is known for. Pistachio-studded varieties and other flavor infusions added to the international flair and indulgence.

Samples of ROYCE’s iconic nama chocolates

This tiny, bustling taquería brings big, bright flavors to the table—fresh salsas, warm tortillas, and lovingly prepared plates that echo the warmth of a family kitchen. Grande Avocado Quesadilla – warm, cheesy, generously filled, deeply satisfying

Review

Tucked inside a large shopping center, it’s an easy spot to miss unless someone points it out—yet it delivers bold flavor, generous veggie portions, and friendly service from the crew behind the counter. Review

They serve up classic platters and wraps—halal, hearty, and full of crunch from freshly chopped vegetables. The chicken has an orange tint, likely from a tikka-style marinade, and the gyro meat is crisp and tender, though both are quite salty. Pairing everything with their sauces and pickles makes it even saltier, which is too bad because the overall flavors are good.

Their yellow rice is my favorite—aromatic with turmeric and cardamom. I could honestly eat a bowl of it on its own. The guys behind the counter are friendly, and overall service has been solid. It’s nice having a NY-style chicken-and-rice spot in town, complete with fresh fruit and vegetable juices to round out the menu. I may swing by again, but the recipes could use a little refinement. Anyway… what are you waiting for? Grab any of the croissants—plain or almond—and make sure they heat it up for ya. Crunch factor sound on and relish in delight! Save me a little crumb in which I may encounter the warm memoir of Marcel Proust… Ciao.”

Body:
Tucked inside the bustling HMart food court, this express version of Jang Guem Tofu & BBQ offers a slimmed-down menu compared to the full-service locations in Bellaire and Sugar Land. While the convenience is great for a quick meal during grocery runs, the service and execution can vary, and some signature elements—like sizzling hot tofu soup and a full spread of banchan—may feel pared back.

Still, certain dishes shine, such as their surprisingly crisp seafood pancake. For diners who already know and love the brand, this location delivers familiar flavors in a more fast-casual format, though it may not fully match the consistency and breadth of the standalone restaurants.

Review

Sara I. (Jan 21, 2020):

“This seems to be an express version of Jang Guem Tofu & BBQ, tucked inside the newer HMart in Katy. Having visited the Bellaire and Sugar Land locations, I’ve always liked their food and menu options.

Service here, however, was dull and lackluster. I ordered tofu soup with mushrooms and asked for kimchi in my soup. When it arrived, it wasn’t bubbling as it normally does in cast-iron bowls. No kimchi in sight, and the flavor lacked the usual sharp, spicy kick. I also noticed there was no egg—normally you crack a raw egg into the hot soup for that creamy binding factor. Without it, the soup felt watery and flat. My friend asked for an egg, but the cashier said they didn’t offer that. Oddly enough, when I went up later, I saw a sign stating you can request an egg. Strange.

Banchan was limited to three small items. The other locations typically offer six. I guess that’s the express trade-off.

The seafood pancake, though, was crisp and well-balanced—probably the best item we had. Not doughy or soggy, and the crunch held up even after a while.

Overall, the meal was just okay. Healthy at least? Many of the other cafeteriastyle stalls serve fried or greasy food, which isn’t my vibe. I’ll likely stick to this HMart for grocery shopping rather than meals.”

Body:
Slowpokes’ Upper Kirby outpost brings the brand’s signature laid-back charm right across from Levy Park. With whimsical animal art, a relaxed aesthetic, and plenty of seating, it’s a breezy place to work, socialize, or unwind before a stroll through the park. Three hours of validated garage parking makes it even more appealing for inner-loopers looking to avoid the usual parking chaos.

The café offers a wide range of drinks—coffee, wine, tea, and house snacks—and while the beans run on the stronger, sharper side, the environment makes lingering here easy. Service is friendly, seating is ample, and both indoor and outdoor options keep the space lively but never overwhelming.

What to Order

Latte (try the rose syrup version)

Cappuccino

House Snacks or Small Plates

Review

Sara I. (Mar 22, 2019): 

“Digging this second location of Slowpokes and liking how it's nestled within the inner loop. The location is stellar—right across Levy park with plenty of parking situated within the garage. You get in a good three hours of free parking within the garage, as long as you get your ticket validated upon leaving the cafe. There's also a bit of outside parking as well within a three hour timeframe.

Upon entering, you'll notice a few whimsical paintings of sloths, snails and turtles. All things cute and slow. Liking the unique concept as well as the decor. Slowpokes has quite a few items in terms of their beverage menu. Plenty of snacks and foodish items as well.

I opted for a latte and asked which sort of syrups they had. The barista recommended a rose latte and that caught my attention rather quickly. Being a fan of rose flavored anything, I went ahead and ordered the latte that she suggested. Service was friendly and the latte was brought promptly to my table. Although I enjoyed my latte, I really couldn't taste any of the rose flavor. The coffee beans are sour and strong here— not the smooth finish type. Latte was generously filled to the brim and I couldn't finish it all.

Next time I'll opt for a cappuccino. Overall I'm diggin' the vibes, music and aesthetic appeal. Nothing hipster, cramped or stuffy about Slowpokes. It's great to have yet another coffee house within Houston—one that I'll definitely frequent.”

Category: Coffee & Tea, Wine Bars

Body:
Asia Blue brings a fresh, modern presence to Tang City Plaza, pairing sleek décor with an open kitchen and a digital menu that makes browsing fun and easy. The atmosphere is polished, bright, and inviting, with warm service and attention to presentation. While the appetizers and tea shine, the entrées—particularly the vegetarian curry noodle soup and laksa—leave room for improvement. Even so, the freshness of the ingredients and the lack of MSG make it worth revisiting, especially as the restaurant continues to establish its footing in this growing food hub.

Review

Sara I. (Dec 21, 2019): 

“I wanted to really love this new spot! The vibe is charming—modern interior, clean and sparkly décor, and an open kitchen where you can watch the chefs at work. The tablet-style menu is a neat touch, making it easy to swipe through photos and descriptions.

We started with vegetarian spring rolls that arrived piping hot and super crisp—definitely made in-house. Paired them with herbal tea served in adorable teapots, which I highly recommend ordering while you wait for your meal.

For mains, I chose the vegetarian curry noodle soup and my friend ordered the laksa. Both dishes were beautifully presented, mine garnished with alfalfa sprouts and plenty of veggies, but the flavors fell flat. The toasted sesame oil seemed to overshadow the curry notes, and I missed the brightness of citrus and spice. My friend felt similarly about the laksa. I added salt and chili to bump it up a bit, and the leftovers actually tasted better the next day.

Still, I appreciated the freshness and the fact that nothing had MSG. Sometimes simple, real ingredients speak louder than anything else. I’m curious to try their Taiwanese-style beef noodle soup next—likely one of their stronger offerings.

Tang City Plaza is the new, up-and-coming hotspot for Sugar Land and Missouri City, so I’ll definitely be back. Noodle soup in this weather is always comforting, and I’m hopeful for an improved experience. Until next time!”

Body:
Bismillah Restaurant & Café has transformed its space with a brighter, cleaner, and more expansive layout—perfect for families, groups, and anyone craving halal comfort food with a South Asian twist. A colorful Houston-themed mural and glowing lighting fixtures give the restaurant a playful-yet-ethereal feel, while the menu blends American classics with Pakistani street-food favorites.

What to Order

Classic Burger – Fresh, melty, satisfying, and far more balanced than the spicier options.

Papdi Chaat – Crisp, sweet-savory, and a crowd-pleasing South Asian classic.

Cajun Fries – Salty, bold, and generously portioned.

Review

Sara I. (Jan 20, 2019):

“I had dinner at Bismillah Café with my mother last night. I specifically came because I heard about the recent renovations—and I hadn’t been in ages. The restaurant is now in a bigger space with a cleaner, brighter look. Plenty of seating for large families and gatherings. There’s even a large painted mural depicting Houston icons—playful and unique. The lighting gives the whole place an ethereal feel.

I don’t normally eat burgers, but I was craving one. I decided on the Diablo burger because it sounded intriguing. I'm a fan of spicy food and figured I could handle it. The lady at the register, who was friendly, recommended it as well. My mom ordered the papdi chaat—an item recently suggested to me, and my mom loves chaat anyway. Both of our orders came out around the same time, and everything tasted fresh.

Unfortunately, the Diablo burger was too spicy for me. The hot sauce had a grainy texture and tasted a bit raw. The burger had all the works—lettuce, onion, tomato—but the cucumbers threw me off. I guess they were added for fusion flair. The Cajun fries that came with it were a heaping pile—salty and overwhelming on top of an already intense burger. I ended up ordering the classic burger because I simply couldn’t eat the first one.

The manager was friendly and brought out the new burger, which was far better. He chatted with us and asked how everything was—something I appreciated, as it made the experience feel homier. The classic burger came with all the basics, minus cucumbers. Melty cheese, ketchup, big bun, big patty—all fresh. I only ate half, but I enjoyed it.

The papdi chaat was crisp and well-balanced, with garbanzo beans and potatoes blanketed in a sweet and savory sauce. Overall, the service was warm, the food fresh, and the dining experience pleasant. I can definitely see myself coming back with family to try other items. I’m not normally in the area, but I recommend everyone visit the newly renovated Bismillah Café. They have something for everyone.”

Body:
A long-loved Houston institution, The Original Marini’s Empanada House delivers warmth, charm, and old-world comfort with every crispy, freshly fried empanada. The interior glows with nostalgic character, and the atmosphere is relaxed and welcoming—plus, the owners’ friendly cats occasionally roam outside, adding even more personality to this neighborhood gem. With an extensive menu spanning savory classics, creative fillings, and sweet dessert blends, there’s truly an empanada for everyone.

What to Order

Beef Picadillo (Beef Gaucho) – Juicy, classic, and the perfect pairing with green chili sauce.

Chicken Poblana (Mole) – Earthy, deep chocolate notes, rich and comforting.

Dessert Empanada: Elvis Melbis – Peanut butter + banana + dulce de leche indulgence.

Reviews

Sara I. (Jan 20, 2019):

“They have cats upon the premises! That's the main reason I dined in here a couple of days ago. Jk. I had dinner here a few nights ago with a good friend. Both of the cats belong to the owners and normally just patrol outside—not inside.

This was my first time at Marini's, though my friend Mike had been here before. The interior is warm and glowing, with plenty of seating. There’s a historical appeal inside Marini’s, and I'm surprised it took me so long to visit.

On a crisp and chilly night, empanadas were just the right items to nosh on. The menu is large and thoroughly categorized—there’s truly an empanada for everyone. I ordered two savory empanadas and one dessert: the chicken poblana (mole), the beef picadillo (beef gaucho), and the Elvis melbis for dessert (peanut butter, banana, dulce de leche).

Everything is made fresh to order, and the taste reflects the quality. Service was prompt and attentive. All three empanadas were delicious—warm, crispy, freshly fried. I couldn’t finish them all and took a few bites to-go. The chicken mole was deep, earthy, and had a unique savory chocolate flavor. My favorite was the beef picadillo—juicy and perfect with the green chili sauce. When it comes to empanadas, I prefer fried over baked, and these were executed beautifully.

The dessert empanada was rich and sweet—the dulce de leche paired nicely with the banana and peanut butter, though I’ll try another flavor next time. With so many options, I look forward to exploring more of the menu. Marini’s also serves soups, salads, and more. Since it carries an Argentinian flair, you’ll find iced yerba mate by the counter. It was watered down in flavor, but still refreshing.

Chill atmosphere and warm food for the soul. Try the Original Marini’s for yourself—it's a Houston classic.

PS – I might just revisit to hang out with the cats.”

Amorino brings a touch of European indulgence to Highland Village, offering artisanal gelato and sorbet crafted with premium ingredients—many imported from around the world. The shop is warm, polished, and often buzzing with people, especially on festive evenings when the surrounding plaza glows with lights and activity. What to Order

Three-Flavor Sorbet Cup – Passionfruit, Black Currant & Raspberry (bright, tart, and intensely fruity).

Chocolate Gelato – Deep, decadent, and perfect for dairy lovers.

Macarons Filled with Gelato – Petite, elegant, and ideal for a sweet add-on.

Review

Sara I. (Dec 31, 2018):

“Ahh! I'm a big fan of sorbet… and this place totally satisfied my craving for all things sorbet related. Amorino serves authentic gelato, waffles, chocolates, coffee beverages, and even pound cakes and macarons. The shop was packed the night I visited—Christmas night—and luckily Amorino was open in this lively part of town. The River Oaks District plaza was glowing with lights and people wandering around.

Amorino has quite a selection of sorbets and gelato, with many of the fruit elements imported from various countries. I chose the smallest cup, which fits three flavors. Without hesitation, I picked the passionfruit, black currant, and raspberry—side by side. I’m so glad I chose them. They were crisp, tart, and full of fresh fruit flavor. Honestly, some of the best sorbet I've ever had!

I definitely want to revisit this cute little shoppe to try their dairy-based gelato—several chocolate flavors caught my eye. Now I understand why Amorino is popular worldwide. It’s a bit on the pricier side, but absolutely worth trying.”

Body:
FIX Coffeebar is a warm, intimate neighborhood café tucked into Montrose—full of wood textures, glowing bulb lights, and the soft hum of students and creatives typing away. Though compact, the space is thoughtfully arranged, with plenty of usable seating and a rotating menu of inventive, house-crafted lattes. FIX thrives on creativity, releasing seasonal flavors and even celebratory drinks like their birthday cake latte (only available in July). If you’re looking for a cozy, community-driven café with personality, this is the spot.

What to Order

Honey Lavender Latte – Balanced, fragrant, creamy, and beautifully blended.

Seasonal Latte Special – Rotating flavors tied to holidays and seasonal inspiration.

Breakfast Taco or Sandwich – Simple, warm pairings to enjoy with their specialty drinks.

Review

Sara I. (Dec 29, 2018):

“I finally had the chance to try out Fix Coffeebar on a rainy mid-week afternoon. Parking is far too few in this part of town—the plaza was packed, and I ended up parking on a corner street, mud everywhere. But alas, I made my trek into the world of caffeine.

Upon entering, you’ll notice the unique layout: warm string lights, wood elements, and a large patterned wood frame against the main wall. Though small, the café is arranged well, with plenty of tables and space for all the students and laptop workers buzzing around on a mid-afternoon weekday.

I was eager to try the birthday cake latte, only to learn it’s only served in July for the café’s anniversary—perfect for my own birthday month anyway. Instead, I opted for the honey lavender latte and was incredibly impressed. I expected the lavender to overpower the honey, but instead they danced together and created a wonderful taste. Creamy, smooth, and not acidic at all.

A few other unique flavors were listed for the winter season. FIX seems to rotate and experiment throughout the year, crafting creative flavor profiles. You can tell this place is passionate about the art + science behind their beverages. Warm, chill vibes, and a friendly barista made the visit even better. Looking forward to returning.”

Body:
The Sephora at Kohl’s in Westchase brings a refreshing twist to the traditional Sephora experience—calmer, cleaner, less crowded, and wonderfully convenient. Open since June 2023, this compact yet well-stocked beauty kiosk sits just inside the Kohl’s entrance, making it an easy stop during a quick errand run or a dedicated beauty shopping trip.

Despite its smaller footprint, the selection mirrors that of larger Sephora locations: fragrances, lotions, makeup, skincare, and gift items all line the shelves. The space feels airy and relaxed, offering the rare pleasure of browsing beauty products without the usual bustle, perfume cloud, or shoulder bumping typical of busier stores.

Customer service shines here, with friendly greetings, helpful answers, and smooth checkout experiences—including the use of account points and seasonal discounts. Nestled in a growing and vibrant part of West Houston, this location adds a modern, accessible beauty option to the neighborhood.

Why You’ll Love It:

Calm, crowd-free shopping environment

Surprisingly large selection for a kiosk-style setup

Quick in-and-out convenience

Friendly and attentive customer service

Easy rewards redemption & holiday promotions

Located in a thriving Westchase retail corridor

Review

Sara I. (Dec 9, 2023 – First to Review):

“So this is a new location of Sephora and they have been open since June 2023. Walk inside Kohl's and you'll spot Sephora's fairly decent sized kiosk store to the left side of the store. I can't remember the last time I visited a Kohl's location, but this made for a good walk and fun visit.

I actually like this location! It's smaller compared to their regular stores yet they pretty much have every item that you would find at regular Sephora stores. Lotions, fragrances and gift items? Check. You'll find it here. This location is less crowded and you'll find what you need within a minute. There aren't people bumping or pushing against you at their other stuffy locations that reek of perfume and blush.

Customer service was great, I was greeted upon visiting and had all my questions answered. Found what that I was looking for and that's all there is to it. I was able to use my account points and they also gave a discount with it being the holidays. Perfect! Although the Galleria location is much closer to me, I can definitely see myself revisiting this one more often.

This new location of Sephora is in one of my favorite parts of town. I love how new businesses continue to develop within this west Houston urban neighborhood.

This business location needs to be revamped with saying ‘now opened’ instead of ‘coming soon.’ You're welcome and enjoy. SYOY.”

Body:
Mazajj Organic Coffee brings a refreshing global warmth to the Galleria/Uptown area, offering an inviting space filled with natural light, stylish décor, and some of the city’s most lovingly crafted chai. With a freshly opened storefront closer to Houston’s inner loop than their Katy location, this café has already become a neighborhood favorite for anyone seeking a cozy, cultural, and aromatic coffeehouse experience.

The atmosphere blends modern elegance with international charm—sunlight pouring through large windows, warm hospitality from the staff, and ambient music that feels transportive. Whether you’re settling in for a quiet morning, an evening wind-down, or a meetup with friends, Mazajj’s ambiance is as memorable as its drinks.

Must-Try Items:

Adeni Chai (light, creamy & perfectly balanced; available by the cup or teapot)

Coffee selections made with quality beans

Desserts including viral Dubai-style chocolate & milk cakes

Complimentary treats during special events or openings

Reviews

Sara I. (Sep 17, 2024 – First to Review, ROTD Dec 22, 2024): 

“Absolutely wonderful interior, lots of indoor lighting as well as natural lighting pouring in through the windows. Great customer service and warm hospitality, thanks guys!

This Mazajj is a lot closer within the inner loop of Houston compared to their Katy location. Their Katy shoppe is just as lovely though, with similar interior deco and piping hot tea.

Choices for teas and beverages are plenty. Want coffee? They've got it. Want tea? They have different styles. My favorite being the Adeni chai. It's not too strong as other spots make it. A bit of a lighter and creamier flavor. I always opt for half sweet and it's perfect. You can get it by the cup or as a teapot. I love their teapot and glassware. Adorable and makes for a cozy morning or evening spent sipping on chai. Warm and exotic music playing in the background makes for such an international vibe. I'm loving how they're situated within the Galleria area. We really needed a spot for authentic chai and Mazajj delivers! They just had their grand opening 2 days ago & already got it down in terms of customer service. Thanks for the complimentary desserts today. So sweet.

Y'all, check out Mazajj and thank me later. Support local and support chai that's made from scratch with true warmth and passion. Try their desserts, viral Dubai chocolate and milk cakes. So good and so worth it. Welcome to the neighborhood!”

Reviews

Sara I. (Aug 22, 2025):

Golem’s Gate in Stafford feels like stepping into a pocket-sized fantasy realm—warm, welcoming, and brimming with imagination. This independently owned mom-and-pop shop is tucked into a quiet corner of town, but inside, it’s vibrant with creativity. Owners Tama and Jason bring heart to the space, offering friendly guidance, recommendations, and an infectious passion for all things tabletop and geekdom.

The shop is stocked with everything a gamer or collector could want: books, miniatures, board games, gaming accessories, plushies, and nostalgic treasures. Whether you're a seasoned Dungeons & Dragons player or a newcomer curious about the world of tabletop adventures, Golem’s Gate invites you to explore, learn, and play. Renting board games is encouraged, and the community atmosphere makes it easy to settle in with friends for a fun escape from the everyday.

Tuesday evening D&D nights bring the shop to life, blending 80s nostalgia with the modern revival of role-playing games. Costumes are welcome, creativity is celebrated, and seasonal holidays—especially Halloween—add extra charm to this already magical spot. Golem’s Gate is the kind of store where phones are forgotten, imaginations take over, and everyone gets to play a character of their choosing.

Why You’ll Love It:

Friendly owners who make newcomers feel at home

Wide selection of games, miniatures, accessories & collectibles

Board game rentals for fun hangouts

Weekly Dungeons & Dragons nights

Nostalgic, fantasy-inspired atmosphere

A great place to unplug, dress up & let imagination roam

Review

You can also rent a board game and play with friends. On Tuesday evenings, the community hosts dungeons and dragons board game nights. A popular game from the 80s that has definitely had a revamp and has its own return into the world of board games.

This is a fun little store where you can really be yourself and tap into your imagination. Dressing up in costumes is allowed and you can play the role of any character that comes to mind. Body:
Slim Chickens is one of those spots you see scattered across Houston—often enticing enough to spark curiosity and high expectations. This Pearland visit, however, delivered a mixed experience: a few standout bites, a few letdowns, and a whole lot of room for improvement. While the concept is promising and the menu broad, not everything hit the mark this time around.

The fried mushrooms were the star of the meal—crispy, warm, and full of satisfying texture. Unfortunately, the rest of the plate didn’t follow suit. The tenders lacked crispness, the fries leaned soft rather than crunchy, and the Texas toast was serviceable but unremarkable. The much-hyped Slims sauce, said to resemble Cane’s, leaned more toward creamy tomato soup than tangy dipping bliss, making it a surprise mismatch for the meal. To top it off, the ranch—requested as a backup savior—never made it into the to-go bag.

Still, Slim Chickens offers a wide selection of sandwiches, wraps, and comforting desserts, leaving the door open for a possible revisit at another location. And for dessert lovers, the pudding jars and cheesecake cups may be the hidden gems worth exploring—especially on a hot Texas day.

Hit or Miss Menu Notes: 

Hits:

Fried mushrooms — warm, crispy & delicious

Misses:

Soft fries

Not-so-crispy tenders

Slims sauce (unexpectedly tomato-forward)

Missing ranch from the order

Worth Trying Next Time:

Sandwiches & wraps

Pudding jars & cheesecake desserts

Reviews

Sara I. (Jul 18, 2023):

“Hmm Slim Chickens! More like the bare bones of it. A place that I had high expectations for, but to be honest, those expectations fell flat upon first sight and bite.

I was excited to try this spot and have noticed it in different parts of Houston but happened to be out in the city of Pears and found it out of happenstance. Twas' evening time and the hunger pangs began for a snack. Something not too heavy, but not too light. My initial thoughts were to visit Canes because I was craving their sauce and tenders, but didn't know which side of Pearland it was at. Slims popped up during my excursion and I thought.. well why not? I've seen this spot before so let’s give it a shot.

Ordered their simple meal of tenders that came with fries and texas toast. Also ordered their fried mushrooms as well. The fried mushrooms were bomb! Incredibly warm and crispy. They had good texture and taste. I wish I could say the same for the rest of my meal, but everything else was OK (fries and tenders). The tenders weren't that crispy, maybe because of all that buttermilk batter? They were also a bit small. Fries weren't crispy, mostly soft. Texas toast was buttery and garlicky, it was average in taste.

I was excited to try their Slims sauce, which I was told was similar to Canes. At least that's what the drive thru staff said. With excitement I asked for 2 orders of their Slims sauce. To my surprise, it did not taste anything similar to Canes sauce. Instead it was very creamy and tomato flavored in taste. Almost like a cream of tomato soup which did not pair well with any of the items that were ordered. I also asked for ranch sauce as well which they forgot to add to my order when I left - that would have been the saving grace to those tenders.

With a plethora of sauce that this place has to offer, I'm sure that I would have a better experience with a different flavor profile. But will I be back? I'm not too sure. I do like how they offer other items on their menu such as sandwiches and wraps. Might visit another location within the Houston area. I was just left unimpressed. Thankfully the meal wasn't as salty or aggressively fried in flavor as other fast foods spots. Slim' ranking for this spot. But might revisit if having a hankering for some tenders. Unless I'm cravin' for another kinda sauce. Until next time.

PS - they are serving up cheesecake desserts & various pudding jar desserts... perhaps something sweeter and cooling in this heat would be nice.”

[PERMANENTLY CLOSED - Store No Longer Operating] 

A warm summer evening set the stage for an intimate and unforgettable chef’s table experience at Yi Peng Thai Dining in CityCentre. What many expected to be a traditional Thai dinner transformed into a sophisticated parade of artisanal small plates, each crafted with bold flavors, rich textures, and a sense of culinary storytelling.

From the moment the dishes began arriving—one after another in elegant progression—the night took on an electric, joyful energy. The short ribs and crispy chicken were standout favorites, decadent without being heavy, balanced by refreshing sips of sweet Thai tea and fresh coconut water lightly iced with slivers of coconut meat.

Chef Jett brought charisma and passion to the table, engaging guests with lively conversation and insights into Thai cuisine. Meeting him, along with his wife and the talented culinary team, added a personal touch to an already immersive dining experience. Their hospitality, warmth, and cultural pride elevated the evening into something far more meaningful than a simple dinner.

The event sparked wanderlust—visions of Thailand, fragrant penang curry, and kaffir lime leaves drifting through the mind long after dessert. Equally delightful was reconnecting with longtime friends and celebrating the evolution of Houston’s food community, where creative and culturally rich gatherings continue to flourish.

Event Highlights:

Artisanal Thai small plates

Slow-braised short ribs

Crispy chicken with bold seasoning

Sweet Thai tea & fresh chilled coconut water

Intimate conversations with Chef Jett

A lively, cozy summer-night atmosphere

Review

Sara I. (Aug 18, 2022):

“Well. What can I say? All my favorite platinum folk already wrote essays upon essays about our grandeur Thai inspired evening in City Centre. It was a cosy summer night as we noshed upon food that was as big & bold with flavor, as our conversations were.

I adored the bold and spunky energy at the table—full of laughter, honesty, and depth. I kept thinking we would eat typical Thai cuisine that night. But that was far from our reality… we were gifted with artisanal small plated meals that were decadent yet rich in taste. My favorites were the short ribs and crispy chicken. Thai tea was quite sweet yet refreshing in between savory meals. Their fresh coconut water was great as well. A bit of coconut meat and lightly iced, it was perfect in this summer season.

Chef Jett was enthusiastic, energetic and fun to speak with. His name is quite huge in this city and it was lovely to finally meet him. His wife and the rest of the culinary team were friendly and informative as well. Thanks to the Thai cultural ministry in their initiative to feed us and tickle our taste-buds & minds.

Now I have a strong longing and impulse to visit Thailand and nosh on penang curry that's sprinkled with just the right amount of kaffir lime leaves. Aside from my wanderlust daydream, I had a great evening catching up with old-school friends. With summer finally ending (I think), it was a great initiative catching up and learning about prospective events and the growth of the community.

Much has changed in the past decade... nostalgia of days gone by… but so much growth and fun still ahead. Cheers!

PS — Thanks for the lippy balm, mints, and other cute little gifts. The remembrance of a fun night will linger longer than the taste of those mints.”

Teapresso Bar in Sugar Land brings a Hawaiian-inspired twist to the local café scene, offering Kona coffee, milk teas, hot beverages, and customizable drinks with organic coffee beans—something not easily found in this part of town. With warm wooden tables, bright interiors, and plenty of seating, it’s a convenient place to study, work, or wind down with a drink.

However, the experience can be hit-or-miss. Once known for friendly service and quality drinks, this location has seen a noticeable decline in customer care, atmosphere, and consistency. Prices have crept up, and the staff’s demeanor has grown increasingly aloof. Still, for locals seeking real milk (not powdered creamer) and solid coffee options, Teapresso Bar remains one of the few alternatives in Sugar Land.

The café continues to shine in its cleanliness, available seating, and steady drink lineup. But with a little more warmth and attentiveness, it could easily return to its former charm—especially in a city craving more unique coffee and tea destinations.

What to Order:

Organic coffee beverages

Tapioca drinks & milk teas

Kona coffee specialties

Light snacks & hot drinks

Atmosphere Notes:

Bright, clean interior

Board games & seating for laptops/work

Can get loud during drink preparation

Review

Sara I. (Jan 11, 2023): 

“This spot was unusually warm today and the service was mediocre at best; which seems to be the case lately. I've always liked Teapresso and really dig the location out in the Heights.. (if it's still around). But this location in the heart of Sugar Land could do way better. They were great when they first started out.. which was about 4 years ago. Since then the service has gone downhill and the drinks are steep in price.

The young lady at the front never smiles and seems to be irritated at any cost. Nonetheless, some of the drinks are still okay and it's one of the few spots where you can actually get a decent cup of coffee in Sugar Land. Simply because you have an option for choosing organic coffee beans and actual milk in your drinks. I always steer clear from non-dairy creamer and crap coffee.

I appreciate the fact that we have a Hawaiian style cafe in town that specializes in tapioca drinks, Kona coffee and a few other items. They have snacks as well as a few hot beverages. Plenty of seating with warm wooden tables and board games as well. It's a decent spot to get some work done or work on anything on your laptop. It can get loud at times because they're obviously making drinks in the corner.

All in all, it's a good spot in the area, especially with limited coffee choices (c'mon Sugar Land!). A bit bleak at times.. hoping they can regain their charm. Plus side? Always clean and bright inside.”

So far with this location? Unimpressed and left much to be desired. This location is super skimpy with their portions and the price point is heavy. For two bowls, 1 bread and 1 green tea, you'll shell out about $30 and leave feeling a bit underwhelmed. Not sure why they are so skimpy with their portions and their service. Body:
Jang Guem Tofu & BBQ has long been a dependable Sugar Land spot for hearty Korean comfort food—piping hot tofu soups, sizzling bulgogi, and a spread of banchan to round out the experience. Over the years, the menu has shifted, and though many dishes remain flavorful and satisfying, service quality has noticeably declined, leaving loyal diners conflicted.

The tofu soups, while warm, fresh, and deeply comforting, have grown increasingly salty. The once-favorite kimchi dumplings—formerly crisp, clean, and made purely of kimchi—are no longer available, replaced by versions mixed with pork and presented with a dismissive explanation. Vegetarian dumplings now fall into the “just okay” category. Meanwhile, blaring music and cold, condescending service dampen the dining experience, especially when simple requests like banchan refills become a challenge.

Still, the restaurant has its strengths: bulgogi arrives sizzling on stone plates, portions remain generous, and certain dishes retain the flavors that longtime guests once loved. For those nearby, Jang Guem may still be a convenient go-to—but with hopes that the service and attention to detail return to the welcoming warmth it once offered.

What Stands Out (Good & Bad): Hits:

Flavorful tofu soups (though salty)

Piping hot bulgogi on stone iron platters

Generous portions

Misses:

Confrontational, dismissive service

Loud, disruptive music

Decline in dumpling quality

Difficult to request banchan refills

Review

Sara I. (Mar 30, 2023): 

“Decent food, terrible service. I've been dining here for years and the menu has gone through a few changes. I used to love their kimchi dumplings that were made purely out of kimchi and nothing else. They used to be crisp, warm and delightful. Back when the restaurant used to give a damn. I asked if I could order that and noticed it's no longer on the menu. They mentioned that it's always mixed with pork. Negative! Sure, maybe your new updated menu, but take a look at your menu from 3 years ago.

The waiter spoke with a cold and condescending attitude. I thought to myself, why argue with someone that has barely worked here for that long? Ordered the vegetarian dumplings instead. Mediocre.

Moving on. I ordered the usual tofu soups that I like getting from here. Sure their soups are good, but definitely on the salty side. Body:
Tønsberg Brygge sits at the heart of Norway’s oldest town—a place steeped in Viking history, maritime heritage, and quiet Scandinavian charm. The waterfront is a picturesque blend of cobblestone streets, historic boats, crisp coastal air, and cafés that line the serene pier. Whether you’re exploring the town’s deep cultural roots or simply wandering along the water, the brygge captures the tranquil, introspective beauty of Norwegian life.

The town itself is layered with history: Viking origins from the 9th century, important trading routes, and solemn stories preserved in its old cemetery, which holds war graves from the Battle of Jutland. Yet despite its historical weight, Tønsberg feels light and peaceful—a place where the days move slowly, the water mirrors the sky, and reflection feels natural.

What to Experience at Tønsberg Brygge

Tranquil waterfront views along the pier

Cobblestone streets near the shopping district

Seasonal farmers markets with fresh, local seafood

Historical boat launches during the holiday season

Cafés and restaurants lining the water

A quiet, small-town atmosphere perfect for reflection

Review

Sara I. (Feb 10, 2022): 

“Tønsberg is quite a beautiful little town—historical and considered to be the oldest town in Norway. Founded by Vikings in the 9th century, it later became an important trading center. Tonsberg Old Cemetery even contains 22 war graves from the First World War, 14 of them unidentified, all naval casualties from the Battle of Jutland in 1916.

The town is charming with its cobblestone streets, especially near the shopping district. I lived here back in 2017 for about half a year, and visiting the brygge (pier) was always a tranquil escape. Many restaurants line the pier, some offering diverse cuisine. Food in Norway wasn’t my favorite overall, but there was a decent Indian restaurant by the water. Local seafood was fresh and often displayed at the farmers market.

The pier would be freezing in autumn and winter. During the holiday season, townsfolk launch their old historical boats—an incredible sight. Many cafés and restaurants close early, and grocery stores were closed on Sundays, which was a bit of a culture shock as an American. Yet these differences brought introspection and deep personal growth. The icy, glasslike water felt like a mirror for self-reflection.

I may have been on the outside looking in, but it was a beautiful, ponderous ride. I recommend visiting the pier and experiencing this quiet, elegant town.”

Tucked inside a row of unassuming office-style buildings near Chimney Rock, Java Pura is one of Houston’s most meaningful hidden gems. This isn’t a café—it’s a working roastery, a coffee lab, and a hub for true bean obsessives. You’ll spot their beans at Urban Harvest Farmers Market, Central Market, and at catered events across the city. Visiting in person feels a bit like stepping behind the curtain into the scientific and artistic core of Houston’s coffee culture.

Here, freshness is everything. The team roasts beans onsite, packages them with care, and pours genuine passion into every batch. You won’t find latte art, but you will find people eager to talk origins, roast levels, equipment, and method. If you’re a home brewer ready to upgrade your morning ritual, this place is a must-stop during business hours.

Review

Sara I. (Jan 29, 2020):

“A gem of a coffee roaster headquartered in Gulfton, near Chimney Rock. It’s a bit difficult to find—just a row of plain office buildings—but that adds to the adventure of locating this coffee lab.

Java Pura is the local soul of the best coffee beans in Houston. You’ll find their products at Urban Harvest farmers market, Central Market, or at various catered events. This isn’t a coffee shop, so don’t expect a barista or latte art. Instead, you’ll meet folks who are incredibly passionate about their beans. They’re friendly and will offer a tour if you’re interested.

I visited a friend here and loved seeing their machines and products up close. Beans are roasted in-house, carefully packaged, and shipped across the city. You can purchase beans here during business hours—fresh, aromatic, and full of character. Grind at home to preserve that flavor.

Java Pura truly represents what it means to support local. Their heart shows through their beans, their packaging, and their dedication to the craft. Once you make the switch, you’ll never go back to Folgers. What’s in your cup?”

Fresh, juicy, bright, and made with real ingredients — Mr. Wish offers a refreshing break from the heavy, creamer-based milk teas found at many shops. This Taiwanese import is all about fresh-pressed fruit, fragrant tea, and clean flavors that let natural citrus shine. Aromas of tea, fruit, and warm waffles greet you the moment you enter, setting the tone for a café experience that’s both cozy and energizing.

Lowering the sweetness level lets the tart, natural flavors come through, making each drink light, crisp, and refreshing. Their in-house waffles add the perfect complement: warm, crisp, simple, and comforting. With patient service and a bright, welcoming atmosphere, Mr. Wish brings a unique charm to Houston’s Chinatown.

What to Order

Wish Special Fruit Tea – A signature blend of fresh-pressed citrus and chopped fruit; vibrant and refreshing.

Custard Waffle Cake – Warm, crisp, made to order; a lightly sweet pairing for any fruit tea.

Grapefruit Green Tea – Tart, fragrant, and best enjoyed with reduced sugar.

Review

Sara I. (Oct 8, 2019): 

“They say dairy does the body good. But I'm not too sure about that. Sometimes over doing it with milk tea leaves ya' belly bloated and hankering for something lighter. Most of these milk teas are questionable as well. Non-dairy creamer? No thank you.

Let's shine the spotlight on fruit tea. & I'm not talking about any kind of fruit tea.. (Let's forgo the teas made with sappy chemical laden syrups). I'm talking about the type that's super fresh, citrusy and bright. Juicy juice that's pressed right on the spot. Mr. Wish has quite a fantastic selection of fresh pressed juice. But they mix it in with tea.. & chopped fruit.. so you've got yourself a winning combination.

Upon walking into Mr. Wish cafe you can smell the aroma of various citrus, tea and waffles.

There are plenty of citrus teas to choose from. All of em bright and sunshiny. You can lower the sugar content down to 60%.. that way you can enjoy the tart flavors of the juice. Nothing too sweet is ever good. Try the waffles that are made in house. They are warm and crisp. I chose the custard waffles and they were filling and tasty. Piping hot.. so wait until they cool down a bit.

Mr. Wish is a bright little cafe that is unique in many aspects. Imported straight from Taiwan.. so these guys know what they're doing. Warm and patient service. A vibrant, joy-filled celebration set inside the Children’s Museum, this lively gathering blended nostalgia, music, local food, and community connection. The space buzzed with energy—interactive exhibits, familiar faces, new introductions, and an atmosphere that felt like one big reunion. Local vendors brought their A-game with fresh desserts, flavorful bites, and warm hospitality, turning the evening into a festive showcase of Houston’s culinary diversity.

Event Highlights

Local Dessert Showcase – Tres leches, gelato, cookies, bundt cakes, and more.

El Bolillo Bakery Cakes – Fresh, rich, and impressively well-made.

Interactive Museum Venue – Playful, engaging, and nostalgic.

Review

Sara I. (Sep 27, 2019): 

“Happy buzz' day! What a funtastic event at the Children's Museum of all places! Last year’s gathering was at the Health Museum, and these museum-style celebrations are always interactive and fun for everyone.

The food vendors were warm and welcoming. I was able to try most of the offerings thanks to arriving at just the right time. Both cakes provided by El Bolillo Bakery were fresh and tasty. It's hard to find a good tres leches cake.. even within Houston. & They nailed it! The owner and manager were humble and friendly; we spoke of all things postres. There was a large variety of desserts at this event—from gelato to cookies and bundt cakes—each created by local businesses. My sweet tooth was brimming with joy.

The music was jamming! I lost my mind when I heard George Michael! Woosh. It was lovely reconnecting with friends. It felt like one big reunion, with plenty of new faces too. As someone semi retired from writing about events, I’ve really seen the community grow immensely. Making local friends is one of the best parts of attending gatherings like this.

Thank you to the organizers for connecting me with genuine folk. After a decade of attending events like these, it’s heartwarming to see how things evolve. Fifteen years later… and we can pretty much check in to any part of the world. Does anyone remember the days where we mostly wrote our reviews through a computer? Haha. Review
